entities.summary:
Amazasp II of Iberia was a king (mepe) of Iberia, ruling from 185 to 189 CE, and the last in the P'arnavaziani line according to medieval Georgian chronicles. He was a son and successor of P'arsman III, who is believed to have ruled in the latter quarter of the 2nd century. Amazasp II's reign is notable for its significance in the history of Iberia, where he played a crucial role in the country's political landscape. His rule was marked by the continued struggle for power among the various factions of the P'arnavaziani dynasty.

Amazasp II's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the P'arnavaziani dynasty on the politics of Iberia, even after his death in 189 CE. The dynasty's line of succession was disrupted, leading to a period of instability and power struggles that would last for centuries. Despite this, Amazasp II's reign remains an important chapter in the history of Iberia, providing valuable insights into the country's political and social dynamics during the 2nd century CE.

Amazasp II's significance extends beyond his own reign, as his rule contributed to the broader trends of the 2nd century CE, including the rise of Christianity and the decline of the Roman Empire. His reign also had a lasting impact on the cultural and economic development of Iberia, shaping the country's identity and informing its relationships with neighboring regions.

The legacy of Amazasp II can be seen in the many historical records that survive to this day, including the medieval Georgian chronicles that detail his reign. These records provide a unique window into the past, offering insights into the politics, culture, and society of Iberia during the 2nd century CE.

One of the most striking aspects of Amazasp II's reign is the limited information available about his personal life. Despite being a king, he is often overlooked in historical accounts of the 2nd century CE, with many sources focusing instead on the more prominent figures of the time.
